title: Chance: {{term:certain}}, possible, {{term:impossible}}
summary: Pick counters from a bag, spin a spinner and roll a dice. Say whether each event is certain, possible or impossible.
guide: This studio follows Iran's Year 2–3 lessons on chance: a bag of counters, a spinner and a dice. Your child guesses first, then tests the guess and looks at the results table. In England this is enrichment: probability is not in the KS2 curriculum.

The three key words: certain means it happens every time. Possible means it might happen or might not. Impossible means it never happens. A common mistake is to think that "most of them" means "certain". Missions 2 and 3 work on this.

The last mission writes a {{term:probability}} as a fraction: 1 way out of 6 {{term:equally-likely}} ways is {{frac:1/6}}. Results change a little each time, and that is normal. With more rolls, the results get closer to {{frac:1/6}}.

engine.event-red-or-white: A red or a white counter comes out.
engine.instruction-place: Put each sentence on the line.

what-can-come-out.title: Which colours could come out?
what-can-come-out.prompt: This bag has 5 red counters and 1 white counter. Without looking, we take one counter out. Which colours could it be? Tap all of them.
what-can-come-out.hint: Look in the bag. Which colours are in it? You can also pick a few counters and see.
what-can-come-out.success: Well done! The counter is either red or white. There are no other colours in the bag.
what-can-come-out.why: Before you take a counter out, can you say exactly which colour it will be? Why?
what-can-come-out.model: No. There are more red counters, so red has a better {{term:chance}}. But the white counter is in the bag too, and it might come out. We only know it will be red or white.

feedback.not-in-bag: There are no blue or green counters in the bag. Something that isn't in the bag can't come out.
feedback.space-missing: You missed a colour. There is only one white counter, but it could come out too.
feedback.space-empty: Tap the colours that could come out.

certain-possible-impossible.title: Certain, possible or impossible?
certain-possible-impossible.prompt: Same bag: 5 red counters and 1 white counter. We take one counter out. Put each sentence on the line: impossible, possible or certain?
certain-possible-impossible.hint: Certain means it happens every time. Impossible means never. Possible means sometimes yes, sometimes no. Pick 10 counters and see.
certain-possible-impossible.success: Well done! Blue is impossible. Red is possible. White is possible too. "Red or white" is certain.
certain-possible-impossible.why: Sara says: "Getting red is certain, because most of the counters are red." Is she right? Why?
certain-possible-impossible.model: No. Red is more likely, but it isn't certain, because the white counter could come out. Certain means every single time.

feedback.most-not-all: Most of the counters are red, but not all of them. The white one could come out. So red is not certain. It is possible.
feedback.one-is-enough: There is only one white counter, but that one could still come out. So it is not impossible.
feedback.no-blue: There are no blue counters in the bag. So getting blue is impossible.
feedback.only-these: The bag holds only red and white counters. Whatever comes out is red or white. So this is certain.
feedback.scale-unplaced: Put every sentence on the line. One is still left.
feedback.scale-high: One sentence is in the wrong place. Look in the bag again.
feedback.scale-low: One sentence is in the wrong place. Look in the bag again.

make-it-certain.title: Make it certain!
make-it-certain.prompt: This bag has red, blue and green counters. Add or take away counters so that getting a red counter is certain.
make-it-certain.hint: Certain means red comes out every time. Which counters could come out instead of red?
make-it-certain.success: Well done! Now there are only red counters in the bag, so red comes out every time. Pick 10 and see.
make-it-certain.why: Ali says: "If we put in 8 red counters and 1 blue counter, red is certain." Is he right? Why?
make-it-certain.model: No. With 8 red counters red is very likely, but the 1 blue counter could still come out. For red to be certain, no other colour can be in the bag.

feedback.too-unlikely: There is still a counter that isn't red in the bag. It could come out.
feedback.empty-bag: The bag is empty! Nothing can come out of an empty bag. Put in at least one red counter.

which-colour.title: Which colour is most likely?
which-colour.prompt: We spin the spinner until the arrow stops on a colour. Guess first: which colour is the arrow most likely to stop on? Tap it. Then spin 10 times.
which-colour.hint: Count the parts. How many parts are blue? How many are green? How many are red?
which-colour.success: Well done! 4 of the 8 parts are blue. Blue covers the most space, so the arrow stops on blue most often.
which-colour.why: If you spin 10 more times, will your table be exactly the same as before? Why?
which-colour.model: No, we can't know. Any colour could come up on each spin. But blue usually comes up most, because it covers more of the spinner.

feedback.smallest: Red is only 1 part out of 8. Red has the smallest chance!
feedback.close: Green has 3 parts. Is there a colour with more parts? Count them.
feedback.choose-wrong: Count the parts of each colour.
feedback.choose-empty: First tap the colour you guess.
feedback.few-trials: Test your guess: spin at least 10 times.

roll-a-six.title: The chance of rolling a 6
roll-a-six.prompt: A dice has 6 faces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. Every face is {{term:equally-likely}}. What fraction of all the ways is rolling a 6? Write the fraction. Then roll 100 times and see.
roll-a-six.hint: How many ways can the dice land? How many of them are a 6? 1 way out of 6.
roll-a-six.success: Well done! 1 way out of 6: the probability of rolling a 6 is {{frac:1/6}}.
roll-a-six.why: Sara rolled the dice 6 times and never got a 6. Does that mean rolling a 6 is impossible? Why?
roll-a-six.model: No. 6 is one of the faces, so it is possible. In a few rolls it might not come up. But if we roll many times, about 1 roll in every 6 is a 6.

feedback.upside-down: Your fraction is upside down. Top: how many ways give a 6? Bottom: how many ways are there in all?
feedback.five-others: A dice has 6 faces, not 5. The 6 itself is one of the ways.
feedback.not-six: That is the fraction of ways that don't give a 6. We want rolling a 6.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Only 1 face shows a 6.
feedback.too-small: Too small. 1 way out of how many? Count all the faces.
feedback.empty: Write the fraction: top and bottom.
